financials_interim.notes: COMPANY (standalone holding-entity) basis. Revenue here is not comparable to a normal operating company's -- it is intercompany/management-fee-type revenue from subsidiaries (main asset is 'Investment in Subsidiaries', Rs.19,261,726k). total_liabilities = non-current (518,112) + current (6,090,573) = 6,608,685 (filing does not print a Company-level total-liabilities subtotal directly, derived by summation). short_term_borrowings = current Interest-Bearing Loans and Borrowings (2,540,524) + Bank Overdraft (220,946) = 2,761,470. capex = PPE purchases (540) + intangible asset investment (4,740) = 5,280.

Hemas Holdings PLC, diversified conglomerate (Consumer Brands, Life Sciences, Hospitals, Mobility, Strategic Investments segments -- reporting structure changed 1 April 2026 to split the former Healthcare segment into Hospitals and Life Sciences; comparatives re-presented, no impact on prior reported totals). operating_profit = 'Operating Profit' (1,627,432), the filing's own subtotal after Share of Results of Equity Accounted Investees. finance_costs = 'Finance Cost' (345,561, a standalone P&L line, distinct from the Share of JV Results which is included above the operating-profit line). short_term_borrowings = current 'Interest-Bearing Loans and Borrowings' (2,238,346) + 'Bank Overdraft' (6,179,278) = 8,417,624; long_term_borrowings = non-current 'Interest-Bearing Loans and Borrowings' (3,282,281). capex = 'Purchase of Property, Plant and Equipment' (617,889) + 'Investment in Intangible Assets' (7,916) = 625,805. EPS cross-check: 937,024k / 2,995,985,015 shares = 0.3128 ~= disclosed 0.31 -- ties. No column-swap issues found. This filing includes an unusually detailed management commentary with segment-level EBITDA/earnings tables (pages 2-7), used directly for the driver attribution below.

interim_updates.note_text: Hemas Holdings' Group revenue was roughly flat YoY (+0.9% to Rs.28.77bn) for Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026), but EBITDA fell 14.1% to Rs.2.26bn, EBIT fell 21.2% to Rs.1.63bn, and earnings attributable to equity holders fell 21.4% to Rs.937mn -- a genuine margin story, per management's own attribution to the Middle East conflict's spillover into Sri Lanka (petrol/diesel prices over 40% higher YoY, LKR down 8% YoY/5% QoQ) pushing net operating costs up 9% YoY, with Selling & Distribution costs (+12.3% YoY, driven by logistics/fuel/freight) accounting for over half of the increase. By segment: Life Sciences (Rs.16.11bn revenue, -3.8% YoY) was hit hardest -- EBITDA -23.1% and earnings -21.5% -- because pharmaceutical prices are NMRA-regulated and could not immediately reflect LKR depreciation and higher import costs; Consumer Brands revenue grew 5.9% but EBITDA fell 23.0% and earnings fell 28.8% as cost pass-through lagged, particularly for the Learning (stationery) and HPC Sri Lanka sub-units. Hospitals grew more resiliently (revenue +11.0%, EBITDA +7.1%, earnings +4.2%) despite a patient-mix shift toward lower-margin communicable-disease/dengue admissions. Mobility was the standout, more than doubling earnings (+116.0% to Rs.320mn) on Evergreen port cargo throughput growth of 28.5% YoY as the Middle East crisis diverted regional shipping volume to Sri Lanka. A further, separately-quantified drag came from the Leisure JV: the Share of Results of Equity Accounted Investees loss nearly quadrupled to Rs.205.6mn (from Rs.51.4mn), which management attributes explicitly to LKR depreciation raising finance costs on the JV's USD borrowings -- this loss sits within the 'Strategic Investments' segment, whose segment PBT worsened to -Rs.670.95mn from -Rs.640.43mn. Higher finance income (net cash-positive Group benefiting from higher interest rates) partly offset these pressures, with net finance cost actually falling 5.4% YoY despite the currency headwinds.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one (e.g. 31 March 2026) has been collected for HHL -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. Segment-level figures above (EBITDA, earnings, margins) are taken directly from management's own segment tables in the filing (pages 3-6), which report on a different basis (EBITDA/earnings) than the consolidated P&L line items (operating profit, PBT) captured in financial_statements -- both are the filing's own disclosed figures, not independently derived, and are not directly additive to each other.
interim_updates.takeaway: This is a genuine margin-compression quarter, not an accounting artefact: management's own disclosure traces it to a specific, external, quantified cause (Middle East conflict -> fuel/freight cost spikes and 8% YoY LKR depreciation) transmitted asymmetrically across segments -- hardest in Life Sciences (regulated pricing lag) and Consumer Brands (selective, incomplete pass-through), largely absorbed in Hospitals, and actually a net positive for Mobility (regional shipping diversion). The Leisure JV loss (nearly 4x YoY) is a distinct, separately-disclosed drag tied to USD-denominated JV borrowings, not part of the operating segments above.
operational_highlights: Group revenue +0.9% YoY to Rs.28.77bn; EBITDA -14.1% to Rs.2.26bn; EBIT -21.2% to Rs.1.63bn; earnings attributable to equity holders -21.4% to Rs.937mn

Life Sciences (largest segment, Rs.16.11bn revenue) hit hardest: revenue -3.8%, EBITDA -23.1%, earnings -21.5% -- NMRA-regulated pharma pricing could not immediately reflect LKR depreciation/import cost inflation

Consumer Brands revenue +5.9% but EBITDA -23.0% and earnings -28.8% as cost pass-through lagged (Beauty/Baby Care categories grew double-digit, but Home Care and Learning stationery margins compressed)
Hospitals grew resiliently (revenue +11.0%, EBITDA +7.1%, earnings +4.2%) despite a patient-mix shift toward lower-margin dengue/communicable-disease admissions; Cath lab admissions +84% YoY
Mobility earnings more than doubled (+116.0% to Rs.320mn) on Evergreen port cargo throughput +28.5% YoY, as the Middle East crisis diverted regional shipping volume to Sri Lanka

Share of Results of Equity Accounted Investees (the Leisure JV) loss nearly quadrupled to Rs.205.6mn (from Rs.51.4mn) -- management attributes this explicitly to LKR depreciation raising finance costs on the JV's USD borrowings
Selling & Distribution costs +12.3% YoY (fuel/freight/logistics), accounting for over half of the Group's 9% YoY rise in net operating costs, per management's own quantification
key_drivers: Life Sciences segment: EBITDA -23.1% YoY (Rs.1,120mn) driven by regulated pharmaceutical pricing lagging LKR depreciation -- the NMRA's pricing formula now includes an exchange-rate adjustment mechanism (beyond a 5% threshold) but revisions still lag the approval process, so margin recovery is expected only gradually

Consumer Brands segment: EBITDA -23.0% YoY (Rs.685mn) as selective/partial price increases (to protect volumes) left the Group absorbing part of the cost inflation; HPC Sri Lanka operating margin fell 2.5pp YoY specifically

Strategic Investments segment (Leisure JV): Share of Equity-Accounted Investee loss -Rs.205.6mn (from -Rs.51.4mn, +300% per the filing), explicitly attributed by management to LKR depreciation increasing USD-borrowing finance costs at the JV -- a distinct, quantifiable driver separate from the four operating segments

Mobility segment (Evergreen port operations): earnings +116.0% YoY on cargo throughput +28.5%, driven by Middle East conflict-related shipping diversion to Sri Lanka and rising freight rates -- the one segment where the same geopolitical shock was a net positive
